u0: No duty is currently outstanding: the siren does not need switching off, no client is waiting with an untaken order, no taken order is waiting to be served, and no slipped food is waiting to be picked back up. The shop stays live, so a new ring, a new arrival, or a food slip will create a fresh obligation to handle.
u1: The siren is ringing and still needs to be switched off; this is cleared by reaching the switch and toggling it. Nothing else is pending: no order is waiting to be taken or served, and no fallen food needs retrieving. Until the switch is toggled, this duty remains.
u10: A client has arrived with the order not yet taken, and food has just slipped and must be picked up on the very next step. The pickup is due immediately; after that, the order still needs to be taken. The siren is off.
u11: A client has arrived with the order not yet taken, food has just slipped and must be picked up on the very next step, and the siren is ringing and needs to be switched off. The pickup is the immediate obligation, with the order and the siren handled afterwards.
u12: A client's order still needs to be taken, and an order already taken is still waiting to be served. Both duties are outstanding; the siren is off and no fallen food needs retrieving.
u13: A client's order still needs to be taken, an already-taken order still needs to be served, and the siren is ringing and needs to be switched off. All three duties are outstanding, and none has an immediate next-step deadline.
u14: A client's order still needs to be taken, an already-taken order still needs to be served, and food has just slipped and must be picked up on the very next step. The pickup is the immediate obligation; the order duties remain afterwards. The siren is off.
u15: A client's order still needs to be taken, an already-taken order still needs to be served, the siren is ringing and needs switching off, and food that just slipped must be picked up on the very next step. The pickup is the immediate obligation; the rest can follow.
u16: Food slipped and was not picked back up on the very next step, so the immediate-pickup requirement is broken for good. Successful completion is no longer possible.
u2: A client's order has been taken and the client is waiting, so the remaining work is to get food from the pantry, prepare it at the stove, and serve the prepared food. Nothing else is pending: the siren is off and no fallen food is awaiting pickup. A new ring or a food slip would add another duty.
u3: The siren is ringing and needs to be switched off, and a client whose order has been taken is waiting to be served. Either duty can be handled first: toggling the switch clears the siren, and serving the prepared food clears the order. If carried food slips, retrieving it on the very next step becomes an urgent additional duty.
u4: Food has just slipped out of the hands and must be picked up again on the very next step; that is the only outstanding obligation, and the siren is off. Picking it back up clears the duty. Failing to hold food on that next step breaks the requirement for good.
u5: Food has just slipped and must be picked up on the very next step, and the siren is ringing and needs to be switched off. The pickup is the immediate obligation, while the switch can be handled after the food is back in hand. No client order is waiting.
u6: Food has just slipped and must be picked up on the very next step, and a client whose order was taken is still waiting to be served. The pickup is due immediately; afterwards, prepare the food and serve the client. The siren is off.
u7: Food has just slipped and must be picked up on the very next step, the siren is ringing and needs to be switched off, and a taken order is still waiting to be served. The pickup is the immediate obligation, while the siren and the waiting order can be handled afterwards in either order.
u8: A client has arrived and the order has not been taken yet, so the remaining work is to go to the counter and take it. Nothing else is pending: the siren is off, no food has just slipped, and no taken order is awaiting service. Until the order is taken, this duty remains.
u9: A client has arrived and the order has not been taken, and the siren is ringing and needs to be switched off. Both duties are open and can be handled in either order. No food has slipped.
